questions.q: What role does a business unit play that neither a legal entity nor a ledger plays?
options: It is the operational organization that actually processes transactions like invoices and orders
It holds the company's bank account numbers
It defines the chart of accounts segments
It determines corporate tax jurisdiction
questions.explain: The business unit is the operational, transaction-processing structure — the layer that actually performs the work, unlike the legal entity (the legal "who") or the ledger (the accounting book).

questions.q: To how many primary ledgers is a single business unit assigned?
options: Zero — business units never connect to ledgers
Exactly one primary ledger
As many as there are legal entities
A different ledger for every transaction type
questions.explain: A business unit is assigned to exactly one primary ledger, which records the accounting impact of the transactions it processes.

questions.q: Is the relationship between legal entities and business units always strictly one-to-one?
options: No business unit can ever be tied to a legal entity
Yes, always exactly one business unit per legal entity
No — one legal entity can contain several business units, and one business unit can sometimes serve more than one legal entity as a shared service provider
Yes, but only in single-currency configurations
questions.explain: The relationship is flexible in both directions: a legal entity may have multiple business units, and a business unit may act as a shared service provider across legal entities.

questions.q: Why is it a design mistake to treat 'legal entity' and 'business unit' as interchangeable terms?
options: Because legal entities cannot process any transactions ever
Because business units replace the need for a ledger
Because they are actually the same Oracle Fusion object with two names
Because the legal entity addresses legal/statutory obligations while the business unit addresses how operational work is actually organized
questions.explain: Conflating the two causes real design mistakes, since they answer different questions — legal standing versus operational organization.

questions.q: What mechanism, previewed in this lesson and expanded later, controls which company policies (like payment terms or approval limits) apply to a transaction based on its business unit?
options: Cross-validation rules
Reference data sets, assigned to business units
Ledger sets
Legal reporting units
questions.explain: Reference data sets, covered fully in Lesson 12, are assigned to business units and control which policies and rules apply to a given transaction.
